idea-plugin.name: Sightline
idea-plugin.description:
Claude Code inside Android Studio, with reviewable changes and controlled tool execution.

Sightline provides a native Android Studio interface for a locally installed Claude Code CLI.

Use it to:

  • Chat with Claude without leaving Android Studio.
  • Attach files and IDE context, and remove any of it before you send.
  • Review tool requests and proposed changes as diffs before they apply.
  • Stop a turn without losing the conversation, and pick up where you left off.
  • Watch what a subagent is doing inside the task that started it.
  • Run your own Claude Code commands, skills and plugins from the panel.
  • Inspect structured build, test and diagnostic results.

Android-aware. Sightline knows your build variant, connected device, module and running process, so you don't have to explain them. It reads Gradle failures into typed diagnoses, resolves crashes back to the line that threw, picks the tests worth running for what you changed, and audits your merged manifest. Logcat is redacted before it can reach a prompt.

Requires the Claude Code CLI (the claude command), installed and authenticated separately. Sightline does not provide Claude access, does not handle your credentials, and has no login screen or backend of its own.

No telemetry. No analytics, no usage statistics, nothing sent anywhere except to the local claude process you started. Sightline itself writes no transcript; note that the Claude Code CLI keeps its own session history under ~/.claude/projects/, under your account and its own retention rules, which is what lets a conversation resume.

Sightline is an independent project and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Anthropic, JetBrains or Google. "Claude" and "Claude Code" are trademarks of Anthropic; "Android Studio" is a trademark of Google. Both are used only to describe compatibility.

Using Sightline in your work, including commercially, is expressly permitted. Free during the beta. See the licence accompanying this listing.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.9.1 — the same plugin as 0.9.0, published signed. Nothing in the panel changed; 0.9.0 and the two releases before it went out unsigned because the signing step was skipped silently, and the release now refuses to publish an unsigned build. Everything below is the 0.9.0 release, which most people will be coming to from 0.8.1.

0.9.0 — a smaller, faster plugin, and the conversation gets the whole panel.

The Agent Activity Map has been removed. The live graph of files, commands and relationships was the largest and most platform-coupled thing here, and it earned less than it cost. The conversation is now the entire panel — the Chat/Split/Map switch goes with it, since a switch between one view and itself is worse than no control. Nothing in the conversation changed: the status line, the recovered-failure tally and the per-turn summary all run on the same observed build, test and tool events they always did. Sightline also no longer needs the Java or Kotlin plugins to be present at all.

You can see how full the context is. The composer footer now shows context-window usage — 35.4k / 200k · 18% — from the CLI's own reported figures, turning amber past 70% and red past 90%. Click it for /context, the full breakdown by category, which costs no tokens.

A failed turn now has somewhere to go. An error used to be one red line. It is now a card that says what the failure means and offers what is worth doing next — copy the sign-in command, check the sign-in, retry, or copy the full text. An unrecognised error still shows the CLI's own words and explains nothing, rather than guessing.

Plan mode is a document you can edit. A proposed plan renders as Markdown with Approve, Edit plan… and Keep planning. Rewriting the plan sends your version back as Claude's instruction, instead of arguing with it in chat afterwards.

Type @ to reference any file in the project — a ranked file list, filename matches first. The reference is expanded by the CLI, so Claude reads the current file rather than a stale paste. Add Selection to Sightline in the editor's context menu does the same for the lines you have selected.

Deny with a reason. A permission prompt can now redirect the work — "not that, run the tests first" — instead of only blocking it. What you type reaches Claude as the tool's own result.

New, off by default: resume a conversation after a restart. Sightline can remember which Claude session belongs to a project, but only after you accept a dialog that says exactly what is stored: a session id and a date, nothing else — no messages, prompts, file contents or paths. Resuming gives Claude its history back; the panel starts empty, because Sightline stores no transcript and cannot redraw one. Turning it off forgets the id.

A quiet turn says so. If nothing has come back for a while and no tool is running, the transcript tells you how long it has been silent. It stays quiet during builds and test runs, which are supposed to take minutes.

Paste an image even when the clipboard is holding something else too. A browser's "Copy image" carries the picture and its URL, and text takes precedence, so the image could not be reached. Shift+Ctrl+V (Shift+⌘V on macOS) or Actions ▸ Attach image from clipboard now takes the image; an ordinary paste that steps over one says so.

Fixed: slash commands typed into the composer were being billed as prompts. A command only runs when it is the first thing in the message, and in an Android project the context block was going in front of it — so /context, /model and the rest quietly became ordinary paid turns that answered something else. Commands now go out on their own, and picking one from the actions menu puts it at the front of what you have typed rather than the end.

Conversation text size is now yours to set (80–200% of the IDE font), and the tool window asks for attention when Claude is blocked on you while the panel is hidden.
